newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sets rates for new 10-year RRSP bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canada sets rates for new 10-year RRSP bonds.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin on Thursday announced the interest rates for its new savings bond designed for registered retirement savings plans and offering terms of up to 10 years.

The first year rate for the bond will be 2.75 percent and will increase to 8.50 percent in the tenth year of the bond's term. The annual compound rate of return over 10 years based on these rates will be 6.01 percent.
A statement from the minister said daily interest will accrue between the purchase and issue date of the bonds at 2.75 percent per annum.
The new RRSP bond, announced earlier this month, features guaranteed annual interest rates for 10 years with compound interest starting on the first anniversary.
Investors will be able to cash in the bonds each year on the anniversary data and there are no fees associated with the product.

The RRSP bond will be on sale from February 3 to April 1, 1997. The bond will offer two issue dates, March 1 and April 1. The April 1 pricing will be announced in early market. The Ministry of Finance said it is reserving the right to terminate sales at any time.

The new bond is part of a push by the Canadian government to increase the amount of borrowing it does using retail debt instruments such as Canada Savings Bonds. Last year the government created a new agency to boost sales, Canada Investment and Savings, and saw sales of CSBs rise 24 percent to C$5.7 billion.

"The Canada RRSP bond is the first new Government of Canada bond designed for retail buyers in over fifty years and marks another important step in our retail debt initiative," said Martin, in a statement.
